Labels follow GoneBy's own judge rubric: a decision/finding/constraint that shaped the SHIPPED product is relevant; dead ends, superseded choices, and chatter are not. Three duplicate pairs exercise dedup (ids 31-34). This measures judge behavior on a controlled corpus; it is not a real project log.
product: Shipped: roaster-export — a Python CLI plus HTTP endpoint that exports coffee-roast curves from the roaster's log files into Grafana via InfluxDB line protocol. Config lives in YAML; ingest retries use exponential backoff with jitter; transport to the collector is TLS. WebSocket push was designed early and cut for scope.

entries.content: Goal: get roast curves out of the roaster's text logs and onto Grafana dashboards for the QA team.
Explored a full Grafana Alloy pipeline; heavier than needed for one file tail. Probably overkill.
The log format: each roast is one line, bean name, ambient temp, then 'BEAN <probe> <temp> <t>' events every second.
I could write a parser for that with regex.
DECISION: export format is InfluxDB line protocol, not JSON — measured a 4x ingest-cost difference on our metrics vendor's pricing sheet.
FINDING: the roaster log's timestamps are local time with no offset suffix; misreading them shifts every roast event by 2 hours.
DECISION: parser converts log timestamps to UTC explicitly at read time; config carries the roastery timezone.
What about Kafka for durability? Might be nice to have a broker.
No broker — one file tail, one exporter. Kafka is complexity we don't need.
Tried a parquet cache for parsed roasts; nothing downstream consumes columnar data, so it only added a file to manage. Dropped it.
CONSTRAINT: the collector endpoint only accepts TLS on 443; plain HTTP ingest is blocked at the network layer.
DECISION: all ingest goes over HTTPS with the vendor CA bundle pinned in the image.
lunch order? I'm getting a sandwich
DECISION (early): payloads will be JSON POSTs to the ingest API — simple to prototype.
That JSON choice from earlier is now superseded: we switched to line protocol for cost. Keep it in mind when we write the exporter body.
FINDING: the vendor's free tier caps at 10k writes/min, so a 500-roast backfill in one shot would throttle us.
DECISION: backfill streams in batches of 500 points with sleep between, CLI flag --backfill-since.
Fixed a typo in the README: 'roaster-exprot'.
CONSTRAINT: QA dashboards refresh every 30s, so exporter flush interval must stay under 30s or the live curve lags the roast.
Set the default flush to 15s per that constraint.
DECISION: config is one YAML file (roaster-export.yaml) discovered via --config, XDG fallback, env override ROASTER_EXPORT_CONFIG.
Considered TOML; YAML won because the roastery team already writes YAML for Grafana provisioning.
maybe we should add a web ui someday
FINDING: retries against the ingest API hammered it in a tight loop during the outage — thundering herd from all three roasters.
DECISION: retry policy is exponential backoff with jitter, max 8 attempts, then queue to disk for a later drain.
The disk queue path is /var/spool/roaster-export/queue, rotated on drain.
CONSTRAINT: runs on the office's Raspberry Pi 4 collector box — Python only, no JVM sidecar.
Wrote a JVM-based statsd bridge before learning about the Pi constraint. Uninstalled.
The WebSocket design from the first week: live push to dashboards. Do we still want it?
DECISION: WebSocket push CUT from scope — 30s dashboard refresh makes sub-second push unnecessary; the exporter stays a simple loop.

FINDING: probe readings sometimes arrive with 60s stalls when the roaster firmware logs buffer fills; dashboards must not gap-fill silently.
DECISION: exporter emits a staleness annotation point when no reading for >90s.
Added a --version flag.
REMINDER: open items after shipping — per-roaster auth tokens, and a soak test on the Pi.
I think the roast curve looks prettier with the smooth line option. Not sure.
DECISION: the HTTP endpoint (/metrics/roasts, JSON) is read-only status + last-export error log for ops; ingest itself stays line-protocol.
Tested the exporter against a fake collector with mitmproxy; TLS pinning behaved as designed.
FINDING: ambient temp field is only present on roast start lines; parser must treat its absence as normal, not an error.
Refactored variable names in parser.py for readability.
Ship it. roaster-export v1 merged: CLI + HTTP status endpoint + line-protocol ingest from YAML config, backoff+jitter retries over TLS.
